final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and instead narrowed the claim using the same record. That reframing is relevant to tone and scope, but it does not cure the underlying compliance defect. A caveated certification position could be appropriate only if the caveat were itself policy-bounded and satisfied the required predicate, such as an actual disclosure, an approved risk acceptance, or a final determination that disclosure is not required. None of those is in evidence. On the present record, the unresolved material limitation for a named launch use case remains noncompliant, even if the Actor no longer argues for clean no-disclosure compliance.
remaining_concerns: Admissible evidence still shows a 1.5-point evaluation gap in the emergency shelter placement segment, and that segment is a named launch use case tied to two nonprofit commitments.
Policy says a weakness affecting a named launch use case is material, and low-volume or non-core labeling does not resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist.
The record still contains no evidence of the required pre-launch disclosure, no approved risk-acceptance record, and no resolution of the gap before launch.
Legal review remains open, so the relevant compliance predicate is unresolved.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch posture but do not satisfy the specific disclosure-or-approval requirement for this material limitation.
